faqs.a:
(a)
All abandoned, lost, or unclaimed property, and all property that is no longer being
               held as evidence pursuant to
section 62-94
shall be disposed of as follows:
(1)
Last known owner determined by custodian.
If, following examination of the property and those public records readily available
               to the custodian, the custodian is able to identify the owner of the property, the
               custodian shall notify the owner. Such notice shall contain a description of the property,
               a statement that the custodian is holding the property, and that, if the owner does
               not make claim to the property within 30 days of the date of the notice, any claim
               of ownership shall be waived, and the property shall be deemed forfeited and it shall
               become the sole property of the city. In addition, the notice shall state the place
               at which the property may be claimed. The notice shall state that the owner, in claiming
               the property, must provide photo identification to the custodian prior to release
               of any property to the owner. Notwithstanding the above, the last known owner may
               file a claim for property after it has been posted on the police department website
               and within the time given for filing of claims after such posting.
(2)
No last known owner determined.
If, following examination of the property and those public records readily available
               to the custodian, the custodian is unable to determine the identity of the owner,
               the property shall be deemed considered abandoned, lost, or unclaimed.
(3)
Procedure.
For any property not claimed by the last known owner within 30 days of notice, and
               for all other property deemed abandoned, lost, or unclaimed, the custodian may cause
               a notice to be published on the police department's website. The notice shall include
               a description of the property and last known owner of the property, if applicable.
               The notice shall contain a statement that the custodian is holding the property and
               the place at which the property may be claimed. The notice shall state that the owner,
               in claiming the property, must provide proof of ownership acceptable to the custodian
               based on any applicable police department policy, and provide photo identification
               to the custodian prior to release of any property to the owner. Finally, the notice
               shall state that if no one comes forward within 30 days of the posting of the notice,
               any claim of ownership shall be deemed to be waived, the property shall be deemed
               forfeited, and it shall become the sole property of the city.
(i)
The custodian shall determine which, if any, items of property shall be posted on
               the website. This determination shall be made in accordance with any applicable police
               department policy.
(4)
Form of claim.
Any claim for property shall be on such form or forms as shall be provided by the
               custodian, shall be in writing, and shall be signed by the claimant. The custodian
               may make any claim form available on the police department's website.
(5)
Evaluation of claim.
Each claim received by the custodian within the claim period as set forth herein
               shall be evaluated by the custodian, who shall review the claim document(s) submitted,
               and may consult city records, other readily available public records or other documentation,
               and may consult with other persons who may have knowledge of the situation as may
               be required in investigating the validity of such claim. The custodian may at any
               time during the evaluation period request additional supporting documentation from
               the claimant.
(i)
The custodian shall, within 30 days of receiving a claim, notify the claimant that
               the claim has been accepted, denied, or accepted in part and denied in part, except
               that if the nature of the claim is such that more than 30 days are required to investigate
               the claim or otherwise make a determination, the custodian shall notify the claimant
               of this fact, and shall give the claimant the expected date the claim will be resolved.
               Any denial notice shall state that the item or property will be held for 30 days from
               the date of the notice to allow for appeal of the custodian's decision in accordance
               with
section 62-95
(a)(9), and then distributed or otherwise disposed of in accordance with the custodian's
               decision.
(6)
Competing claims.
In the event that more than one person files a claim for the same property, the custodian
               shall resolve any competing claims. The custodian may, in the course of resolving
               the competing claims, request additional supporting documentation, or consult with
               any knowledgeable person(s) for assistance. The custodian shall notify each claimant
               of the resolution of the claim. The notice shall state that the disputed property
               will be held for 30 days from the date of the notice to allow for appeal of the custodian's
               decision in accordance with
section 62-95
(a)(9), and then distributed or otherwise disposed of in accordance with the custodian's
               decision. In the alternative, the custodian may resolve competing claims by depositing
               any or all of the disputed property with the registry of the district court in an
               interpleader or other action. Should the custodian petition any court to resolve any
               disputed claims, the custodian shall notify each claimant of this action.
(7)
Distribution.
In all cases, once the custodian has resolved a claim and there are no statutory
               or other prohibitions on release of the property, the property shall be disbursed
               or distributed as soon as is practicable.
(8)
Procedure when claims are denied.
In the event that any claim or all claims filed are denied in whole or in part the
               remaining property shall become the sole property of the city and any claim to such
               property shall be deemed forfeited.
(9)
Appeal of denial of claim.
Any legal action challenging the denial by the custodian of a claim in whole or in
               part, or any legal action challenging a forfeiture, shall be filed pursuant to Rule
               106 of the Colorado Rules of Civil Procedure within 30 days after the date of the
               custodian's notice, or after the date of the custodian's notification of the impending
               forfeiture, or shall be forever barred. If any legal action is timely filed, the property
               shall be disbursed or distributed by the custodian pursuant to the order of the court
               having jurisdiction over such claim.
(10)
Bond forfeited.
The forfeiture of any bond that is posted with the municipal court shall be done
               in compliance with municipal court standards.
(11)
Disposition.
If property held in custody remains unclaimed 30 days after such property is no longer
               required to be held in evidence pursuant to
section 62-94
, or 30 days after such property has come into the possession of the custodian, or
               30 days after the mailing of any notice provided for in this section, whichever is
               the longest time, such property may be retained by the police department for use in
               training or for other official purposes, or disposed of from time-to-time by the custodian
               as follows:
(i)
Any such unclaimed property may be transferred to the custody of the director who
               is authorized to retain and use or dispose of any property that becomes the property
               of the city under the provisions of this article. In the alternative, the custodian
               may deliver to the director an itemized inventory of property, after which the custodian
               may facilitate pickup or delivery of the items to the contractor responsible for auctioning
               surplus city property, or to another authorized party. Any such sale or other disposition
               of unclaimed property shall occur in accordance with the provisions of the purchasing
               and contracts ordinance.
(12)
Status of purchaser.
The purchaser of any unclaimed property that is sold by the city pursuant to the
               provisions of this article takes the property free of any and all claims of the owner
               or previous holder thereof and of all persons claiming through or under them.
(13)
Items of minimal value.
Notwithstanding any other provision of this article to the contrary, certain items
               of property having a minimal value which are not suitable for sale, and which can
               be used for the public's benefit, may be donated to a recognized charitable institution
               or nonprofit organization, if approved by the city manager, without having to comply
               with the provisions of this article. Such items may include, but are not necessarily
               limited to: toys, bicycles, clothing, bedding, and personal care items.
(14)
Appraisal of property.
The custodian may seek information about any item's value, or have any item appraised.
(15)
Cash.
Notwithstanding any other provision of this article, any cash that comes into the
               possession of the custodian may be placed into an interest bearing account, which
               interest shall accrue to the benefit of the city. The custodian shall work to determine
               the last known owner or otherwise evaluate any claims to the cash. If a determination
               of ownership is made, the custodian shall pay to the owner by check in U.S. funds,
               the amount originally deposited in the matter. If no rightful owner is determined,
               the city may retain the cash for use by the city, unless ordered to the contrary by
               a court of competent jurisdiction, or if such cash is subject to forfeiture under
               state or federal law, then the city shall disburse the cash in accordance with such
               court order or forfeiture law.
(16)
Notice.
All notices referred to in this article shall be in writing, be done by United States
               first class mail, postage prepaid, and sent to the last known address of the owner
               of the property as shown on readily available public records, or in the case of a
               claimant, to the address provided by the claimant.
(i)
Notices placed on the police department's website shall be made in accordance with
               any applicable city or police department policy.
(
Ord. No. 4238, § 1, 12-6-2010
)
